This happened under time pressure approaching the 90-minute global run backstop. File-type inspection, a content-indicator string scan, and a sampled JSON-parse check WERE run (see integrity_scan below) and found nothing concerning, but the full malware scan was skipped entirely due to running out of time budget before the 90-minute backstop, and the rename-before-scan ordering error means even a clean scan result would not have satisfied this run's own stated finalization sequence. Data is real and verified by git's own integrity mechanisms (fsck, tree hash) - this is not a data-quality partial, it's a process-compliance partial. Flagging honestly rather than mislabeling as complete.

status_change_note_appended_2026-08-01.append_only_declaration: APPEND ONLY. Every field above this note stands unchanged, including protocol_compliance: ordering_violated, the acquisition block's malware_scan.attempted: false, report_only_mode_confirmed: false, and the deliberate contradiction between the acquisition block and the later post_acquisition_verification. Those remain the record of what went wrong. The single field modified anywhere in this manifest is snapshot_status. This snapshot's FILES were not touched.
status_change_note_appended_2026-08-01.why: Re-acquired without a .git directory, per docs/workorder-task2-source1-reacquisition.md. This snapshot's DATA is genuine - the successor cloned the identical upstream head commit 4764726896973204a798325ed0f9ed7253e995e5, so both hold the same upstream state. What this snapshot carries that the successor does not is a live .git directory: 33 files, four active Git LFS hooks, a working remote, and pack objects. That makes a snapshot defined as inert data non-inert - a git pull inside it would mutate data described as immutable, and the LFS hooks fire on git operations.
two_reasons_it_was_replaced_rather_than_: Removing .git from this finalized snapshot would have mutated a sealed snapshot in order to enforce the rule about not mutating sealed snapshots.

Git mutates its own internals on read - index refresh, gc, repack - so any hash manifest covering .git internals drifts with nobody touching the data. A sealed snapshot that fails its own integrity check for no real reason is worse than no check, because it teaches everyone to ignore the alarm.
status_change_note_appended_2026-08-01.gate_5_finding_resolved_not_waived: This snapshot's 2026-08-01 re-gate failed gate 5 on facebook.github.io, found in a stock .git/hooks/fsmonitor-watchman.sample. NO allowlist entry was added. The successor simply has no .git, and its gate 5 found zero unexpected domains and zero http(s) URLs of any kind across all 28,960 files. The finding was resolved by removing the cause, not by widening the gate.
status_change_note_appended_2026-08-01.what_this_snapshot_still_is: Genuine data at a verified upstream commit, fully hashed and malware-scanned after the fact. It is superseded, not repudiated. Its provenance fields - git_head_commit, git_branch, git_commit_date, git_origin_url and git_origin_url_verified_exact_match - are what made re-acquisition safe to verify against, and they remain the reason the successor could confirm upstream had not moved.
